source_title: U.K. PM Andy Burnham's trip to India could take place soon: British Envoy
source_excerpt: New Delhi British Prime Minister Andy Burnham is keen to visit India and a trip could take place soon, a top U.K. diplomat said on Thursday (October 29, 2026), highlighting the growing partnership between the two countries. Speaking to PTI, Acting British High Commissioner to India Ben Mellor said Mr. Burnham had conveyed his desire to visit India during a conversation with Prime Minister Narendra Modi after taking office. “I know that Prime Minister Andy Burnham is very keen to come to India," Mr. Mellor said. Mr. Burnham was appointed as prime minister on July 20 this year. On the India-U.K. economic ties, Mr. Mellor expressed confidence that the two countries would surpass their target of doubling bilateral trade as their economies continue to grow. The Free Trade Agreement (FTA) came into force 100 days ago. But actually it was signed just over a year ago. Since then we've already seen new deals worth 12 billion pounds, he said. India and the U.K. are aiming to double bilateral trade to around $120 billion by 2030. Mr. Mellor also said the U.K. remained strongly welcoming to Indian businesses and investors, noting that Indian investors had been the second-largest source of new investment projects in the country over the past several years. Modi, Burnham discuss trade, technology, Hormuz over phone Modi, Burnham discuss trade, technology, Hormuz over phone The U.K. counterpart Andy Burnham set out his ambitions to further enhance the U.K.-India relationship Modi, Burnham discuss trade, technology, Hormuz over phone storyline 1 He said the India-U.K. Free Trade Agreement (FTA) had further improved the environment for businesses seeking to invest, trade and work across the two countries. “Just two weeks ago, seven mayors from the UK and one local authority brought a large business delegation of over 200 businesses to India to come and look for partners that they could work with,” Mr. Mellor said. He said the measures announced in Wednesday's U.K. Budget had reinforced that approach by seeking to make the British economy predictable and attractive for investment. Asked how the Budget would help ordinary British households facing cost-of-living pressures, Mr. Mellor said Chancellor John Healey had announced measures aimed at supporting households, particularly by addressing high energy costs. “Most households in the UK will benefit from 100 pounds off their energy bills next year,” he said. Mr. Mellor said the Budget also sought to put the British economy on a stronger footing through tight fiscal rules while addressing economic headwinds arising from the conflict in West Asia. "There is also a ready headroom of some 15 billion pounds to deal with any crisis that may come along in the future," he said. "I think we can be very confident that the steps the Chancellor announced yesterday have put the UK economy on very stable footing whatever the future holds," Mr. Mellor added.
